# Flatpak

The Flatpak is the installer for Linux. There are two parts, both built by the `Build` workflow (`flatpak-x64`, `flatpak-arm64`):

* `io.github.xaymar.BlitzLLVM`: the compiler and the tools (`blitzcc`, `blitz-format`, `blitz-tidy`), on the freedesktop SDK because `blitzcc` hands programs to clang (which comes from the SDK extension `org.freedesktop.Sdk.Extension.llvm21`).
* `io.github.xaymar.BlitzLLVM.Runtime`: the shared libraries that programs load when they run (FFmpeg for movies, the AVIF, JPEG XL, TIFF and WebP codecs, Opus and Ogg), with their licenses. The compiler and every game ask for it as an extension, so Flatpak installs it once, however many games are installed.

```sh
flatpak install --user --bundle blitzllvm-<version>-flatpak-x64-runtime.flatpak
flatpak install --user --bundle blitzllvm-<version>-flatpak-x64.flatpak
flatpak run io.github.xaymar.BlitzLLVM hello.bb
```

Run the other tools with `flatpak run --command=blitz-format io.github.xaymar.BlitzLLVM file.bb`. The compiler gets your home folder (`flatpak override --user --filesystem=host io.github.xaymar.BlitzLLVM` for more), the network, sound, a window (Wayland or X11) and the GPU and controllers. Programs that `blitzcc` runs for you run inside the sandbox too.

## Shipping your game

`packaging/flatpak/game-template` is a template for releasing a compiled game as a Flatpak of its own, on `org.freedesktop.Platform` with the runtime extension. The game is only its executable and its media: the libraries are not copied next to it (the compiler Flatpak tells `blitzcc` that the extension provides them, see `system-libraries.txt`), and other games share the one copy of the extension.

```sh
./build.sh mygame.bb media/     # compiles inside the compiler Flatpak, packs com.example.MyGame.flatpak
```

* `/app` is read-only, so `launcher.sh` runs the game with a writable working directory in the game's own data folder (`~/.var/app/<id>/data`) where the shipped files appear as links. Saves land there.
* The game gets a window, sound, GPU and controllers, and the network only if it needs it (remove `--share=network` otherwise). It does not get the player's files.
* The compile uses `-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc`. SDL3 is still linked into each game (about the same size as one codec), and `libblitzphysics.so` is copied next to games that use collisions or picking; moving both into the extension is possible later.

## How it is built

Like the snap, `flatpak-builder` does not build BlitzLLVM: the `Build` job builds it once with every `BLITZ_SYSTEM_*` option OFF (the freedesktop runtime has none of the libraries that a distribution's package takes from the system), installs it with prefix `/app`, and `packaging/flatpak/split.sh` moves the shared libraries into the extension and marks them as provided by the system. Flathub is not possible with this: it builds from source without network access.
